transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-21 15:00:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Riya Patel, Sofia Kim, Markus Vogel, Priya Shah, Liam O'Connor, Ana Ruiz

Auto-summary: customer sees accuracy drop after AWQ-int8 conversion; run hypotheses and plan experiments inside customer VPC.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, joining me is riya our quant SE and sofia from support. how's everyone?
[00:12] Markus Vogel: good thanks—short morning for me. so we pushed AWQ-int8 yesterday and by the next morning we saw a 6 to 12 percent drop in our F1 on entity extraction, mostly on long-context docs, short prompts look mostly unchanged.
[00:28] Riya Patel: hi all. the goal here is to figure out whether this is intrinsic to AWQ quant noise or a serving interaction (kv cache, batching, runtime kernel selection). we'll propose a sequence of reproducible experiments.
[00:40] Priya Shah: to add infra context: we run a 13B finetuned model on dedicated nodes in our VPC, traffic ~150 qps, typical seq length ~512 but we have spiky tails to ~2k. adaptive batching windows are non-zero, we use prefix caching aggressively.
[00:55] Jordan Lee: that profile is important; longer sequences can push different attention kernels and change kv-cache warm/cold behavior, both of which can amplify quantization differences.
[01:06] Liam O'Connor: quick security note: all test artifacts must remain inside our VPC and we need full audit logs. we can't share raw PII, hashed inputs only.
[01:15] Riya Patel: that's fine—our plan is to provide a dockerized harness you run in your subnet, it writes logs to your S3 and we ask only for aggregated diffs or hashes unless you opt-in.
[01:27] Markus Vogel: our conversion used the AWQ defaults from the open repo; we didn't tune per-layer clips. could defaults explain the regression?
[01:36] Riya Patel: possibly. AWQ aims for aggressive weight quant with per-channel scaling but defaults can be suboptimal for some layers. GPTQ tends to do a better job at preserving per-layer error at cost of conversion/compute.
[01:47] Ana Ruiz: also curious about mixed-precision—some ops we keep fp16, others int8, could that distribution shift cause downstream differences?
[01:55] Riya Patel: yes mixed-precision gating can change activation distributions. another hypothesis: sense that with kv reuse, small rounding error accumulates across cached prefixes and shows up for long documents.
[02:08] Jordan Lee: we'll map hypotheses: H1 layerwise sensitivity, H2 kv-cache accumulation, H3 batching/micro-batch kernel path divergence, H4 mixed-precision mismatch.
[02:18] Priya Shah: about micro-batching—we aggregate by length in 50ms windows, sometimes requests get micro-batched with different seqs, which might change attention scheduling.
[02:27] Riya Patel: exactly; that can trigger different kernel code-paths (e.g., fused attention vs non-fused) and numerics differ slightly, magnified by quantization.
[02:37] Markus Vogel: how do we reproduce deterministically? our quick local tests weren't isolating kv.
[02:43] Riya Patel: recommended triage: (1) deterministic offline forward-pass compare AWQ vs GPTQ with identical RNG seeds and single-thread no batching; (2) KV on/off: include tests with kv disabled and with sticky kv across segments; (3) runtime reproduction with your VPC config and adaptive batching so we can see production mixing.
[03:02] Jordan Lee: metrics we'll capture: per-layer MSE to fp16 baseline, per-token perplexity delta, and F1 deltas on your golden set. we'll also capture activation norms for suspect layers.
[03:12] Ana Ruiz: ok, for logging we can capture means+vars per layer and hashed inputs, that should be fine.
[03:18] Priya Shah: will the harness need GPU drivers or special kernels for fp8? our on-prem nodes are a mix of A100 gen1 and gen3.
[03:27] Riya Patel: fp8 support differs; A100 gen3 has better fp8 kernel paths, gen1 may fallback to slower implementations. we'll include cpu-fallback flags and recommendations. for initial tests stick with int8 AWQ and GPTQ on gen3 if possible, but include a gen1 run to see perf delta.
[03:43] Jordan Lee: regarding fallback strategies — we can implement per-route policies: default AWQ, but for routes flagged high-precision or long-seq route to GPTQ. also can do user-level canary sampling.
[03:55] Markus Vogel: cost/latency tradeoffs? if we route long seq to GPTQ we accept higher latency, that's ok for some routes.
[04:02] Riya Patel: yes tradeoff is predictable: GPTQ exhibits higher token cost and slightly higher latency in many setups. AWQ gives largest savings but more variance in accuracy for some inputs.
[04:12] Liam O'Connor: for compliance we need a clear audit trail of each canary and any auto-fallbacks. is that supported in the console?
[04:20] Jordan Lee: yes redirect logs, we can tie canary rollouts to trace ids and store event history, and provide RBAC for who can flip fallbacks.
[04:30] Markus Vogel: short-term wins we can try in 48 hours?
[04:34] Riya Patel: three quick experiments: A) run deterministic single-run AWQ vs GPTQ on 1k examples across short (<=256) and long (>=1024) contexts; B) KV-off test to check if cache reuse is source of drift; C) reduce AWQ clipping params for top suspect layers and re-evaluate. we'll provide suggested clip factors.
[04:55] Ana Ruiz: are there tooling scripts we'd run inside our VPC?
[04:58] Riya Patel: yes we'll hand over a docker image with the harness and a runner script that uploads aggregated diffs to your S3. instructions for redaction and hashing included.
[05:09] Jordan Lee: timeline and owners recap: Riya builds and hands the harness, target run date 2026-11-04, Jordan sends SOC2 + audit docs this week, Markus provides prompt set and metrics by 2026-10-28.
[05:22] Priya Shah: one more ask — can we capture some trace-level info when a regression occurs so we can map back to runtime kernel versions?
[05:29] Sofia Kim: yes we'll include kernel ID, runtime flags, and quant table snapshots in the logs, lightweight so it doesn't bloat artifacts.
[05:38] Markus Vogel: perfect. thanks for the clear plan.
[05:41] Jordan Lee: ok we'll follow up with the docker image, runbook, and calendar invites. thanks everyone.

End of transcript
